payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.

payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show a recognizable frog that was not present in the source image?
node.criteria: Pass if a recognizable frog is visible in the edited image and no recognizable frog is visible in the source image. Fail if no recognizable frog is visible in the edited image, or if the apparent frog was already present in the source. Unknown only if the images do not provide enough visual evidence to judge frog identity or source presence.

node.endpoint: A recognizable frog is added to the image as part of putting a frog in the toilet.
node.necessity: A frog must be added to fulfill the requested change; comparing source and edited images distinguishes an added frog from one already present. This is a necessary aspect of the requested endpoint, not a requirement to limit the number of frogs.

d1_placement: The node’s criterion is already fairly specific, but its conjunctive wording (“overlap or occlusion,” scale/perspective, and contact) may make evaluators apply different thresholds to the same bowl frog. Clarify how these cues jointly support the single semantic judgment—whether it reads as occupying the bowl—and distinguish meaningful bowl-relative depth/occlusion from mere visible overlap or feet touching the interior. In the edited image, the bowl frog is clearly added and located within the opening, while its front-facing, sharply cut-out appearance and weak bowl-relative integration plausibly support either reading; frogs on the lid and floor are not evidence for this check. Preserve that distinction rather than treating any frog in the opening as a pass or requiring photorealism. The two pass traces and three fail traces are all valid, queried, high-confidence observations with no dependency failures, so this is evaluator/criterion ambiguity, not transport or schema failure. The reference “partial” constrains the aggregate only: it is consistent with progress (a frog was added) but does not establish this node’s atomic label. Keep the required binding and avoid forcing a label; make the decision boundary and evidence standard more reproducible, and treat repeated disagreement as a calibration signal rather than proof that the requested edit is absent.
